subject: truck2077
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: futuristic militarized truck from 2077.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk, extremely intricate.
reasoning:
I'm planning the vehicle as a simple static prop without joints, since it's scenery rather than a creature, keeping the module compact but still well-structured.

I'm sketching out dimensions for an 8m military truck with six wheels, and designing a helper function for building boxes and cylinders oriented along different axes. I'm also thinking through color strategy -- using flat colors within the 64-color limit for stripes, emblems, and glow elements, while considering kit-based paints and metal textures for the body panels, keeping in mind that painted surfaces can't emit glow.

Working out wheel and chassis layout...

Still shaping the cab wedge profile...

Adding an armor frame around the slit, then side window planes with slits, a hood with vents, a glowing headlight bar strip, and a heavy front bumper/plow built from boxes.

Now I'm planning bull bar spikes along the bumper, a roof sensor array with radar dish, antennas, magenta light bar, and camera turret, plus an armored cargo container with a top turret, missile pods, rear ramp and lights, hazard-stripe panels, decals, and merged ribs for performance.

I'm setting up a geometry-merging helper that collects boxes by color, applies their transforms, and merges them with BufferGeometryUtils before adding each as a single part.

Still writing batching helpers...

I'm keeping the flat color count low for merged geometries since each distinct color needs its own material, and making sure boxes, cylinders, cones, spheres, and torus shapes all share compatible attributes for merging. For painted panel surfaces like cargo containers, I'll use direct parts rather than merging. Now I'm planning out the SVG textures I need, starting with hazard stripe patterns for warning plates.

Beyond the hazard stripes, I'm listing out the remaining decal textures: a windshield HUD, cyan headlight lenses, a cyber emblem for the cargo sides and doors, side window slits, a neon "ARES-77" display screen, a turret targeting reticle, a "2077" serial stencil, tinted circuit patterns for panels, and tire hub rim spoke textures. I'm designing a reusable decal helper that places a textured plane at a given position and direction, with optional glow/emissive treatment for the illuminated elements.

I'm now working through plane orientation math -- since planes only render front-face, I need separate decals per side, and I'm calculating the viewer's right vector when looking at the truck's left face to make sure text and graphics read in the correct direction relative to the vehicle's front.

Now I'm planning the weapon systems: a roof turret with twin barrels and a sensor glow, a rear missile pod with a 2x3 tube array, and a side-mounted rack, plus underbody details like axles, driveshafts, and differentials.

Beyond that I'm adding exhaust stacks with glowing tips behind the cab for silhouette, fold-out solar/shield plates on the cargo sides, and neon underglow strips in magenta/cyan beneath the chassis, settling on a dark gunmetal and olive-drab color palette for the overall vehicle.

Now I'm placing fender boxes bridging the wheel arches, positioning front wheels beneath the cab and sizing the fender geometry so it extends just beyond the cab's side profile.

I'm checking that the wheel positions don't collide with the cab body—since the tire's inner edge nearly intersects the cab's lower side, I'm raising the chassis so the cab sits above the wheel line like a cab-over design.

Now I'm adding fender boxes above the wheels on the cab sides for visual wheel arches, and sizing the cargo bed to sit above the rear wheel clearance, spanning the rear axle positions.

I'm figuring the chassis frame rails, bed floor height, and overall bed box dimensions, then checking the gap between the cab's rear wall and the bed's front edge to add connecting detail there.

For the overall height I'm reconciling bed top at roughly 2.95 with the turret and antenna stack reaching near 3.9, plus an exhaust stack around 3.6. I'm defining a paneled olive paint material with rivets and mottled texture for the bed and cab surfaces, pulling in the mottle helper from the SDK for the camouflage-style finish.

Now I'm adding diagonal-stripe hazard texture planes on the front and rear bumpers, protruding dark ribs along the container sides every 0.75m, horizontal beams on top, and a raised "gun deck" roof panel with rails and vents. For decoration I'm placing a large side emblem, an "ARES-77" text strip, and a "2077" stencil decal in yellow and black.

I'm positioning ribs on the bed's side panel while checking they don't overlap the emblem decal's z-range, spacing them out at specific z values so the protrusions clear the decal zone and the rear wheel positions.

I'll simplify by keeping the ribs thin and low-profile, with the decal plane sitting just above them so the small gap isn't noticeable from a distance. Now moving to cab details: extruding the cab profile centered on the x-axis with painted thickness, then adding side armor plates as boxes flanking the cab halves.

For windows and seams, I'm positioning the side window plane above the armor plates, checking how the cab wall profile's z-height transitions align with the windshield region so the window sits correctly against the roof geometry.

Now I'm adding a roof plate, a glowing light bar up front with alternating colors, and considering a radar dish on the rear roof using either a lathe shape or a partial sphere for the dish geometry.

Checking the dish outline doesn't self-intersect, then considering tilting the lathe axis so the dish faces up and slightly forward.

Now I'm placing the satellite dish and feed arm at the roof rear, then moving to the cab's front details: the hood fascia, grille decal, glowing headlight and brow-light strips, and bumper geometry positioned within the 2.4-wide front profile.

I'm also shaping the plow blade as a slanted quadrilateral plate extruded across the width, checking that its lowest points still rest near ground level for clearance.

Now I need to work out exactly where the wheel geometry touches the ground — with a 10-segment cylinder the bottom could land on either a flat face or a vertex depending on rotation, so I'm adjusting the wheel center height to keep the floating gap within a small tolerance rather than exactly zero.

Settling on 12 segments with center at .62 gives a near-perfect ground touch either way, so I'm locking that in and moving on to defining the wheel assembly: tire cylinder, hub cylinder, and a glowing torus ring around it.

Now I'm placing the wheels at x=±1.55 facing outward, with bolt details, a rim ring, and an armored hub cover with a cone cap. I'm setting six wheels total for the rear axle pairs, plus mud-guard flaps and fenders overlapping the bed area above the wheels.

Still refining the fender geometry, adding an outer lip plate to suggest a wheel arch, plus tilted wedge pieces at the ends for shaping, before moving on to the chassis rails.

Now I'm laying out the chassis components: side rails with crossmembers, axles running through wheel centers, differential spheres, driveshaft, springs and shocks, plus magenta underglow boxes mounted just below the rails for that glowing effect. I'm also considering adding skirt armor plates between the axles, checking their placement so they don't overlap with the wheel inner radius.

Now I'm computing the gaps between front, mid, and rear wheels to figure out where skirt plates can fit, settling on outer skirt plates with cyan glow edge strips positioned between the cab and bed. I'm also thinking about adding cylindrical fuel tank drums tucked inside the skirts near the chassis rails.

I verify the tank dimensions fit under the bed and cab without clipping, spanning roughly 2 units in length along z. Then I move to designing a roof-mounted gun turret on the bed, with a ring base cylinder and a boxy gunmetal body sitting above it.

Adding dome, barrels, and shroud details...

I'm also planning rear-facing details: an ammo belt feeding into the turret, a glowing-eyed sensor head, and a reticle decal on the turret face. For the bed rear, I want tall antenna rods with glowing tips at the corners, plus a cyberpunk touch -- a holographic "2077" sign panel mounted on a rod, visible from both front and back.

Now I'm detailing the rear door panel with armored decal lines, glowing corner lights, a bumper box, hazard plane, and trailer hitch, plus an "ARES" sign decal. I'm also designing side-mounted missile pods on the bed with a 2x3 grid of dark tube openings on their front faces.

I decide to skip tilting the pods since rotating sub-positions would require extra transform logic, keeping them straight instead, and I'm adding mirror arms with camera boxes and glowing lenses to the cab.

Now I'm placing exhaust stacks behind the cab in the narrow gap between the cab back and bed front, sizing them carefully so they fit without colliding, with glowing orange tips, plus a connector fill box to visually bridge that gap.

For the cab, I'm adding a windshield plane positioned on the sloped front surface with proper offset and orientation so it sits flush and upright, along with vertical armor bars across it.

Now I'm computing the tilt angle for the slope bars so their boxes align with the windshield's slope direction, placing them at symmetric x-offsets plus a center bar, then adding a visor box above the windshield.

I'm also working out the hood geometry, deriving the slope line equation from the roofline to the hood, so I can angle hood vent boxes to match that descending front slope.

Checking headlight placement against the grille width to avoid overlap, then positioning the bumper box and a hazard-stripe plane on its front face. I'm considering dropping the plow idea in favor of a spiked bull bar made from cones mounted along the bumper top.

I'm rotating the cones to point forward, sizing and spacing seven spikes across the bumper front, then adding a winch cylinder with a hook tucked underneath. For the cab I'm adding amber marker lights and thin vertical seam lines on the door at a couple of z positions.

Now I'm placing door plates with seam strips and handle boxes mirrored left and right, plus a small shield emblem decal, then adding mirror arms with glowing cyan camera lenses. Next I'm starting the windshield HUD texture using an SVG overlay.

Writing SVG code...

Still writing texture code...

I'm counting ten total textures and now adding surface details like roof radiators, vents, and swept cable/hose paths running from the turret to the cab, keeping everything in model space since there are no bones to anchor them to.

For the merged batch geometry, I'll apply flat shading and use glow on the resulting part, then tally the distinct flat colors needed — gunmetal, dark, steel, yellow, and a few more — to keep the palette consistent.

Now I'm working through which paint textures each part needs, like mottled olive for the cab, and checking what noise/mottle utilities to import from the builder library for those effects.

Still working out paint logic...

Checking the cab outline points don't self-intersect, tracing a sensible convex path from bottom-left forward to bottom-right, up the front, back along the hood, and closing. With thickness 2.4 the cab spans ±1.2 in x, giving a clean vertical back face. Then I'm sizing and positioning the bed as a box roughly 2.6 wide, 1.5 tall, 5.9 long, placed so its top spans from z -4.3 to 1.6.

Now I'm adding the roof plate and rails on top, plus roof hatches, cooling fans with blades, a turret position, and missile pods, all placed along the bed's z-range with fans positioned near the rear.

I'm catching overlap between the missile pods and the cooling fans, so I'm repositioning the pods closer to center and shifting the fans further back, then adding a holographic sign on a pole at the rear above the fans to avoid clashing with the pods.

I'm now placing antennas, sign support rods, and checking the turret's position relative to the cab roof and radar dish, nudging the turret back slightly so the barrel clears everything cleanly.

With the layout finalized, I'm ready to start writing the actual textures and part code.

Setting up imports for the builder utilities and the helper function that positions and merges colored geometry into batches...

I'm verifying the rotation math for cylinders aligned along different axes before writing the box and cylinder helper functions.

Still writing geometry helpers...

I'm reconsidering whether parts without a bone default safely to root, and thinking it might be safer to add an explicit root joint like "chassis" so rigged models have a guaranteed anchor, possibly adding wheel joints too for future animation support.

Adding wheel joint support...

For the rig itself, I'm skipping a dedicated wheel role and just naming joints like wheelFL directly. I'll add turret joints too — a yaw joint at the turret base and a gun pitch joint near the barrel — attaching the turret ring and body to the yaw bone and the barrel to the pitch bone, while leaving doors out for now.

I'm setting up bone attachments: wheel joints positioned per side (FL/ML/RL on +X, FR/MR/RR on -X) with directional vectors, then explicitly binding non-wheel parts like side panels, decals, extrusions, and sweeps to the body bone since parts would otherwise snap to the nearest joint by default.

Writing wheel builder loop...

Still positioning wheel details...

Still writing decal helper and texture definitions...

Writing windshield SVG with glints, reticle overlay, and HUD text...

Designing the grille, headlight, reticle, and holo display icons...

Adding more color constants and building the chassis section, positioning rails, cab, and bed boxes with their offsets.

I'm checking that the driveshaft, differentials, and rail clearances all stack vertically without colliding, then placing shocks and leaf springs at each wheel position. For the underglow strips, I need to verify their placement doesn't conflict with the fuel tanks mounted lower on the chassis.

Now I'm positioning the twin fuel tanks with their retaining bands along the sides, then starting to think through the skirt panels underneath.

Checking skirt clearance against wheel positions confirms no overlap between front and rear wheels. I'm adding mud flaps behind each wheel as dark boxes positioned at the trailing edge, then moving on to assemble the cab, bed, and remaining pieces while keeping the overall part count manageable.

Now I'm writing the cable sweeps connecting the turret base to the cab roof using catmull-rom curves, plus the roof plate and an alternating magenta/cyan lightbar strip across the top.

Adding radar dish, mast, and feed detail...

Now placing cab antennas with glowing tips, plus mirror arms and glowing lens boxes on either side of the cab.

For the turret, I'm attaching a bone body ring and base cylinders, then building the main turret box in olive tones with a slanted front wedge piece.

Still placing details... sensor box with glow-red lens spheres, side ammo boxes with brass belts, tilted armor plates, and the paired barrel cylinders mounted on the gun bone.

Adding more turret details...

Still working out the roof panel geometry, fan blades, glow ring torus, and edge rails for the turret structure...

Now I'm planning the holo sign with back-to-back decal planes facing opposite directions for visibility, and sketching the rear face layout with door lines, hazard stripe, and glowing red rear light panels.

I'm continuing with rear bumper geometry, a glowing strip, a hitch cylinder, and now mapping out the bed side decals including emblem placement, hazard stripe, and sign plate positioning.

Settling on rib z-positions around 1.45, -0.2, -2.55, and -4.2, with the sign planes positioned to not fully block them, plus a horizontal beam along top and bottom.

Adding glow strips along the bed sides and top, then deciding to skip extra side vents on the bed and place those on cab plates instead. Working through cab side plate placement and door seam details, positioning them relative to the cab's x-boundary.

Now I'm figuring out door seam positions and dimensions, a handle box, an emblem decal, and window placement on the cab side wall—making sure the window sits correctly within the wall's height and depth bounds.

For the front fascia I'm placing a grille decal, headlight boxes within a reasonable width range, and a glowing magenta brow strip, checking that each fits within the cab's front face dimensions without overlapping the seams or handle.

Now I'm adding the lower fascia armor plate, deciding against a hood stripe, and placing a visor box above the windshield that fits under the roofline, then positioning a winch cylinder below the bumper line checked against ground clearance and wheel placement, plus adding a hook and spike cones to round out the front details.

I'm also adding sensor lidar cylinders at the bumper corners with glowing cyan rings, cable sweeps, and exhaust stacks built from layered cylinders for the shaft, shroud grill, cap, and a glowing orange tip, topping out around y 3.46.

I'm checking that the connector fill box between the stacks doesn't overlap with the stack cylinders, then adding rear antennas with bases and tiny glowing spheres at the tips, bringing the overall model height to about 4.4. I'm now writing the cab paint extrusion, confirming the thickness is centered properly, and moving on to the panel parts.

I'm setting up the joint hierarchy for body, turret, and gun, confirming the part signature accepts a texture option and that upward-facing planes default correctly to world Y. I'm also working out how to type the bone parameter so it maps cleanly to the joint records.

I need to keep the root joint constraint in mind — only the first joint lacks a parent — and I'm defining the cable bone sweep along the body. For dirt detailing on the bed, I'm using a noise-based paint function that darkens areas below a wavy threshold height.

Confirming paint functions return valid color inputs, and double-checking that geometries get freshly cloned per wheel loop iteration so instances don't share state. I'm settling on consistent positional helper signatures for box and cylinder primitives, covering color, size, position, rotation, group, and bone name, with the cylinder helper supporting separate top/bottom radii.

I'm verifying degree-to-radian conversion for Euler angles and confirming all primitive geometries are indexed so mergeGeometries works cleanly, while adding a tuple type for positions to satisfy TypeScript strictness. Time to write out the final code now.
